abstract: We have investigated the effects of 10 MeV proton irradiation on the magnetization M and critical current density J/sub c/ of bulk single-crystal YBa/sub 2/Cu/sub 3/O/sub 7-/spl delta// (YBCO) superconducting thick wire filaments produced through laser-heated floating zone (LHFZ) technique. M and J/sub c/ were determined both along the length and perpendicular to the length of the wire. Radiation-induced enhancement of J/sub c/ along the length of the wire was observed while there was a small decrease in J/sub c//spl perp/ to its length. J/sub c/ values along the length of the wire up to /spl sim/1.4/spl times/10/sup 5/ A/cm/sup 2/ at 77 K and /spl sim/1.3/spl times/10/sup 6/ A/cm/sup 2/ at 30 K and in applied magnetic field H=1 T were observed in the irradiated samples. In the unirradiated sample, the difference in magnetization /spl Delta/M at a given field in the magnetic hysteresis loop for increasing and decreasing field applied /spl perp/ to the sample length was observed to depend on the orientation of the sample about its axis. This indicates anisotropy in J/sub c/ along the sample length. This anisotropy increased on irradiation relative to the direction of irradiation. We believe that these J/sub c/ values along the length are amongst the highest published J/sub c/ values for bulk high temperature superconductor (HTS) thick wire filament.

articleTitle: The Nucleus - A Report From The General Chairman Of The 1996 NSS/MIC
abstract: The 1996 Nuclear Science Symposium and Medical Imaging Conference was held between November 3 through November 9, 1996 in Anaheim, California. The conference followed in the footsteps of its predecessors in its success. The meeting, which convened at the Marriott Hotel in Anaheim in sunny Southern California, included technical sessions on a variety of topics on nuclear science, medical imaging, and nuclear power and a series of interesting short courses. Seven hundred sixty six attendees from around the world listened to two hundred eleven oral presentations and reviewed three hundred twenty eight posters covering the full range of symposium topics. The short course program which featured six short courses was attended by one hundred and two students. The conference also enjoyed two workshops, one on FASTCAMAC organized by Satish Dhawan, Yale University and another on the Applications and Methods of Compton Scattering organized by Tumay Turner, UC Riverside. The conference was further enriched by the participation of thirty five commercial exhibitors who presented various products relevant and vital to the attendees.

articleTitle: Foreword
abstract: This section of this issue of the IEEE Transactions on Nuclear Science (TNS) is devoted to the 1996 Medical Imaging Conference (MIC), which was held at the Marriott Hotel in Anaheim, CA, November 7-9,. 1996 in conjunction with the Nuclear Science Symposium (NSS), November 5-7, 1996. The Medical Imaging Conference has been growing in size and stature from a few sessions in the NSS in the late seventies to almost an equal partner with the NSS in the organization and operation of the annual meeting. The Nuclear Medical and Imaging Science Technical Committee, which is the group in charge of the MIC, has evolved from a few people organizing the medical imaging sessions, appointed by the NPSS president, into an elective committee with its own constitution and an elected governing council. It is now appropriate for the MIC to have its peer reviewed work from the annual meeting appear under its own cover in TNS. The June and August issues were handled in this manner this year. Most of the papers that were accepted from the MIC appeared in these issues. However, a number of papers did not complete the review process in time for the August deadline due to some combination of complexity of subject matter, extensive revision requirements, or slow response times on the part of the author and/or the reviewer. In the corning year we will be taking steps to accelerate the review process with the goal of having all reviews finished in time for the June and August issues. Thus, it is likely in the future that only the June and August Issues of the MIC TNS conference issuers will be under separate cover. The MIC manuscripts will be in designated sections of TNS that include regular contributed papers or papers from other conferences.

articleTitle: Outstanding Conference Paper Award
abstract: The recipients of the 1997 IEEE NSREC Outstanding Paper Award are Fred Sexton, Dan Fleetwood, Marty Shaneyfelt, Paul Dodd, and Gerald Hash of Sandia National Laboratories, for their paper entitled, "Single Event Gate Rupture in Thin Gate Oxides."Their paper explores single event gate rupture (SEGR) vulnerability in thin gate oxides representative of advanced technologies. The industry trend toward increasing electric fields as oxide thickness and feature size scale down in advanced technologies raises the concern that SEGR may be a limiting factor for integrated circuits (ICs) in space applications. It has been suggested that, as devices scale to 0.25-μm and below, SEGR by Fe ions will occur, leading to a large increase in catastrophic failures in space hardware. Through a study of SEGR in capacitors and ICs, they found a 1/EcR dependence of critical field to rupture as a function of ion LET, consistent with the work of earlier researchers. Moreover, in this work the increasing dielectric breakdown strength of thin gate oxides leads to a greater than expected resistance to heavy-ion induced rupture that is anticipated to translate into a reduced SEGR vulnerability for advanced technologies, contrary to recent predictions. This suggests that SEGR need not be a limiting factor as future technologies scale into the deep submicron region.
